newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline interims seen dulled by stg.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline interims seen dulled by stg.

text.p: The upward march of the pound is expected to be a major factor damping down the headline performance of British-based drugs giant SmithKline Beecham Plc, which announces second quarter and first-half figures on July 22.

Analysts are forecasting second quarter pre-tax profit of between 360 and 382 million stg, compared with 418 million in the first three months of the year and 342 million stg in the same period a year earlier.
"Currency will be the main thing. The headline (figure) won't look very good, but the underlying will be," said one analyst.
Sterling's strength reduced reported first-quarter earnings growth by around 11 percentage points, and analysts at BZW expect this to have accelerated to 13 points during the second quarter.

On the drugs side, anti-depressant Paxil/Seroxat and anti-biotic Augmentin will continue to be star performers, with both showing strong gains in U.S. prescription figures. Indications about the early performance of heart drug Coreg, launched in the U.S. in the middle of June, will also be watched with interest.

Consumer health, which sells brands like Aquafresh toothpaste and pain killer Panadol, is expected to see a slow down from the 18 percent sales surge registered in the first quarter, which was flattered by the impact of the Nicorette and Nicoderm smoking-cessation products.
The main black spot, Clinical Laboratories, is unlikely to have seen much improvement during the quarter, analysts said.

There has been speculation that SmithKline could follow the lead of its U.S. rival Eli Lilly & Co and write down the value of its U.S. pharmacy benefit manager, DPS, which cost $2.5 in 1994. Many analysts believe the purchase was an expensive mistake.
Last month Lilly wrote down the value its own pharmacy benefit company, PCS, by $2.4 billion to reflect lower-than-expected cash flows.
